title: Don't despair
hookLine: O My servants who have wronged yourselves, don't despair of Allah's mercy, He forgives all sins (39:53)
last: KNOWING ISN'T EQUAL TO NOT KNOWING.

lines: MEN WHO HAD DONE TERRIBLE THINGS.
WHAT YOU SAY IS GOOD, BUT...
cards: A group of men come to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. They've done terrible things: killed many times, and committed adultery many times. They've listened to his message, and they like it.
But they say their problem straight. What you're calling us to is good. If only you could tell us there's a way to make up for what we've done.
They aren't arguing. They're asking whether it's already too late. A report in Sahih al-Bukhari says the answer came as revelation, and one of the verses was this one.

teach.h: O MY SERVANTS: STILL CALLED HIS.
teach.b: Surah Az-Zumar, verse fifty-three. Pickthall: "Say: O My slaves who have been prodigal to their own hurt! Despair not of the mercy of Allah, Who forgiveth all sins. Lo! He is the Forgiving, the Merciful."
Start with the address. Ya 'ibadiya, O My servants. Before a word about what they did, Allah calls them His.
People who have gone too far against their own souls, and still addressed as Mine. The first command isn't do this or do that.
It's: don't despair. La taqnatu. The verb names the despair of someone who has stopped expecting anything, and the verse forbids it before it promises anything else.
Then the promise: He forgives all sins, jami'an, every one of them.
Scholars read this with the very next verse: turn to your Lord and submit to Him before the punishment comes. The door is wide, and the way through it is turning back.

Some early authorities are reported to have called it the most hopeful verse in the Qur'an. And notice who it was for: not people with small slips, but men who had killed. Teachers draw the point out.
If the verse reached them, it reaches the person who skipped their prayers for a month, broke a promise, or fell back into an old habit. In that reading, the danger isn't only the mistake.
It's deciding the mistake is the end.

how: Muslims seek forgiveness by saying astaghfirullah, often many times a day, and many scholars and preachers quote 39:53 to people who feel their sins are too great to be forgiven.

o: trust that every hardship ends within this life
keep a cheerful face for others when life feels hard
never lose hope in Allah's mercy, whatever you've done

s: the verse was revealed for people with only small sins
a report in Bukhari says it answered men who had killed and done worse.
the verse calls wrongdoers My servants before anything else
ya 'ibadiya: they're addressed as His first.
scholars read the verse together with a call to turn back
the next verse says: turn to your Lord and submit to Him.

games.q: men who had done terrible things tell the Prophet: your message is good, but is there any way back for us? what came in answer?
o: first, make up for every wrong.
games.why: don't despair of Allah's mercy: He forgives all sins, with the next verse asking them to turn back to Him.

practice: Think of one good habit you let slip: a prayer, a walk, a call to a parent, this very path if you missed some days. When a voice says it's too late, or you always do this, hear the verse's first words instead: O My servants.
Then choose the smallest way back, not to make up for everything, just to return; if you pray, you can say astaghfirullah.

wordCard.voice: Don't despair. Az-Zumar fifty-three: to people who have wronged themselves, never lose hope in Allah's mercy, for He forgives all sins to those who turn back. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: don't despair, from the root q-n-t, the despair of someone who stops expecting anything.

carryVoice: Your line: never despair of mercy. Even men who had killed were still called His servants. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: Say: O My slaves who have been prodigal to their own hurt! Despair not of the mercy of Allah, Who forgiveth all sins. Lo! He is the Forgiving, the Merciful.
